# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]
name = "material-configurator"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Configurator"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Material Configurator"

[host.inputs]
seat_color = "Configurator.seat_color"
seat_metallic = "Configurator.seat_metallic"
seat_roughness = "Configurator.seat_roughness"
frame_color = "Configurator.frame_color"
frame_metallic = "Configurator.frame_metallic"
frame_roughness = "Configurator.frame_roughness"
stripe_a = "Configurator.stripe_a"
stripe_b = "Configurator.stripe_b"
back_roughness = "Configurator.back_roughness"
sun_intensity = "Configurator.sun_intensity"
```

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

            }

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.

# Task: Two lamps: toggle each one, flip both, switch both off

The scene Demo is drawn from the front with a flat (orthographic) camera. It shows two square lamps, LampA on the left and LampB on the right. A lamp is either off (dark grey, #3a3a3a) or on (yellow, #ffd24a). Both lamps start off.
Make the keyboard control the lamps:
- A press of the A key toggles LampA (off becomes on, on becomes off). A press of the B key toggles LampB.
- A press of the Space bar flips both lamps, each from its own state: a lamp that is on goes off and a lamp that is off goes on. (If the lamps are in different states they are still in different states afterwards.)
- A press of the Enter key switches both lamps off.
Every key press counts and takes effect in the order the presses were made, also when several keys are pressed at the same moment (in the same frame). Without any key press nothing changes. The lamps' shapes and positions, the camera and everything else stay as they are.

These declarations must exist when you are done: Demo.LampA, Demo.LampB

# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]
name = "material-configurator"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Configurator"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Material Configurator"

[host.inputs]
seat_color = "Configurator.seat_color"
seat_metallic = "Configurator.seat_metallic"
seat_roughness = "Configurator.seat_roughness"
frame_color = "Configurator.frame_color"
frame_metallic = "Configurator.frame_metallic"
frame_roughness = "Configurator.frame_roughness"
stripe_a = "Configurator.stripe_a"
stripe_b = "Configurator.stripe_b"
back_roughness = "Configurator.back_roughness"
sun_intensity = "Configurator.sun_intensity"
```

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

        if placed < MAX_PLACED {
            var tint: color = TEAL;
            if placed % 2 == 1 {
                tint = ROSE;
            }
            spawn(
                Pillar {
                    origin: vec3(PLACE_X0 + PLACE_STEP * f32(placed), 0.0, PLACE_Z);
                    height: PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * f32(placed);

```

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.

# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These declarations must exist when you are done: Demo.Panel, Sweep

# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.

# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These declarations must exist when you are done: Demo.Panel, Sweep

# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]
name = "material-configurator"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Configurator"

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

            }

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.

# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.

# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.

# Mtek language guide (v0.1)

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/language-guide.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

- Status: generated from `tools/release-docs/templates/language-guide.md`; `npm run check:release` fails when this file is stale (decision 0100).
- Language version: 0.1.
- Compiler: mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1).
- Every program below is a real file of this repository, copied by the generator. The compiler checks them in its own test suites, so the code on this page cannot drift from the language. The facts in the prose (counts, lists of names) are read from the compiler and the registry.

This guide is a tour. It teaches by showing programs; it does not repeat the rules. For the rules read the [language reference](language-reference.md); for what v0.1 does not do read [limitations](limitations.md); to run something first read [getting started](getting-started.md).

## 1. What a Mtek program is

A Mtek program describes one scene: its entities, its state, the shader stages of its materials and the resources they need, as one checked unit. `mtek build` turns it into JavaScript and WGSL for a runtime on browser WebGPU. The compiler has 168 supported features, listed in Part C of the [reference](language-reference.md#part-c-features-of-this-build-168).

The language has no `while`, no closures, no generics and no user-defined types other than `struct`; the full list of what is refused is in [limitations](limitations.md). The reserved words (30 of them) cannot be used as names even though v0.1 does not use them.

## 2. A project

A project is a directory with an `mtek.toml` and the sources it names:

```toml
[project]
name = "pulse-cube"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Demo"

[build]
target = "web"
title = "Pulse Cube"

[host.inputs]
tint = "Demo.tint"
```

`entry` is the first file; `scene` is the scene the application mounts (one scene per application in v0.1). `[host.inputs]` exposes a piece of scene `state` to the page that embeds the program (section 7).

## 3. A scene

```mtek
scene Demo {
    state speed: f32 = 0.7;
    state tint: color = #6b5cff;

    camera Main {
        position: vec3(0.0, 2.0, 5.0);
        target: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
    }

    entity Cube {
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };
        position: vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0);
        rotation: quat.identity();

        update(dt: f32) {
            self.rotation *= quat.axis_angle(vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), speed * dt);
        }
    }

    on key_down(Key.Space) {
        speed = -speed;
    }
}
```

- `state` is mutable data of the scene.
- `camera Main { ... }` declares a camera. A scene needs exactly one active camera.
- `entity Cube { ... }` declares an entity: a mesh, a material and a transform. Fields are written `name: value;`. A descriptor such as `Box { size: ... }` builds a value of a registry schema.
- `update(dt: f32) { ... }` runs every frame. `self` is the entity.
- `on key_down(Key.Space) { ... }` is an event handler. The events of this build are `collision_enter`, `collision_exit`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `pointer_down`, `pointer_move`, `pointer_up`.

Meshes are generated from descriptors; the schemas of the category `mesh` are `Box`, `Plane`, `Sphere`.

## 4. Types, values and functions

The types of the prelude are `PointerEvent`, `SurfaceInput`, `array`, `bool`, `color`, `entity_ref`, `f32`, `glb_asset`, `i32`, `mat4`, `material`, `mesh`, `quat`, `sampler`, `string`, `texture`, `u32`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`. There is no implicit conversion between them: `f32(x)`, `i32(x)` and `u32(x)` convert explicitly. Integer arithmetic wraps and out-of-range array indices are clamped, identically on the CPU and the GPU; the rules are in the reference (sections 5 and 6 of Part A).

A function is a module item. `fn` is pure; `cpu fn` may also call the CPU-only intrinsics:

```mtek
fn pulse(t: f32) -> f32 {
    return 0.65 + 0.35 * sin(t);
}
```

The intrinsic functions of this build are `abs`, `acos`, `alive`, `asin`, `asset.glb`, `asset.linear_texture`, `asset.texture`, `atan`, `atan2`, `ceil`, `clamp`, `color.linear`, `color.srgb`, `cos`, `cross`, `degrees`, `destroy`, `distance`, `dot`, `exp`, `exp2`, `floor`, `fract`, `inverse_sqrt`, `is_key_down`, `length`, `lighting.pbr`, `log`, `log2`, `mat4.columns`, `mat4.identity`, `mat4.rotation`, `mat4.scale`, `mat4.translation`, `max`, `min`, `mix`, `normalize`, `pow`, `print`, `quat.axis_angle`, `quat.euler`, `quat.identity`, `radians`, `random`, `reflect`, `round`, `sample`, `sampler.linear_clamp`, `sampler.linear_repeat`, `sampler.nearest_clamp`, `sampler.nearest_repeat`, `saturate`, `sign`, `sin`, `smoothstep`, `spawn`, `sqrt`, `step`, `tan`, `texture.black`, `texture.white`, `transpose`, `trunc`.

## 5. Materials and shader code

A material is a typed parameter list and exactly one `fragment` function. The compiler turns the function and every pure function it calls into WGSL; nothing else is compiled to the GPU.

```mtek
material Pulse {
    param tint: color = #6b5cff;
    param phase: f32 = 0.0;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        return color.linear(tint.rgb * pulse(phase), tint.a);
    }
}
```

A material instance sets the parameters in the entity: `material: Pulse { tint: bind(tint); phase: bind(frame.time) };`. The lit built-in materials are `Pbr`, `Unlit`; `lighting.pbr` is available in stage functions:

```mtek
export material Striped {
    param stripe_a: color = #e8e2d0;
    param stripe_b: color = #2a3f5f;
    param bands: f32 = 6.0;
    param metallic: f32 = 0.0;
    param roughness: f32 = 0.6;

    fragment(input: SurfaceInput) -> color {
        let albedo = color.linear(mix(stripe_a.rgb, stripe_b.rgb, stripe(input.uv.y, bands)), 1.0);
        return lighting.pbr(input, albedo, metallic, roughness);
    }
}
```

## 6. Binding

`bind(expression)` makes a field follow an expression every frame, without a handler. A value that changes at run time never creates a pipeline or a shader module: it is written into a uniform buffer (`spec/gpu-layout.md`).

```mtek
    entity Meter {
        position: bind(vec3(-8.0 + (0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered)) * 0.5, 6.0, -3.0));
        scale: bind(vec3(0.4 + 0.5 * f32(entered), 0.4, 0.4));
        mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
        material: Unlit { color: #ffd040 };
    }
```

## 7. Host inputs

`[host.inputs]` of `mtek.toml` maps names to scene `state`. The host page sets them with `app.setInput(name, value)`; the runtime validates each value with a codec. The codecs of this build are `f32`, `i32`, `u32`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `color-hex`, `color-hex-opaque`, `string`.

```toml
[project]
name = "material-configurator"
language = "0.1"
entry = "src/main.mtek"
scene = "Configurator"

## 8. Modules and prefabs

A file is a module. `export` makes an item importable; `import { A, B } from "./path.mtek";` imports by name. There are no wildcards, no aliases and no package imports.

```mtek
// The constants every other module of the showroom shares: the palette, the sizes of a pillar and the row that
// spawned pillars are placed in. Nothing here is a scene or a prefab; it is only imported.

// The colour of the sky behind everything (the scene's clear colour).
export const CLEAR: color = #14181f;

// The palette. Materials, prefabs and the scene all take their colours from here.
export const SLATE: color = #3a4150;

export const STONE: color = #9aa3b5;

export const GOLD: color = #e0a526;

export const TEAL: color = #2f9e8f;

export const ROSE: color = #e0527a;

// The default width of a pillar, in metres.
export const PILLAR_WIDTH: f32 = 0.8;

// The row of pillars that the P key places: `MAX_PLACED` slots, `PLACE_STEP` apart, from `PLACE_X0` on,
// at depth `PLACE_Z`. Pillar number n is `PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT + PLACE_RISE * n` tall.
export const MAX_PLACED: i32 = 4;

export const PLACE_X0: f32 = -2.4;

export const PLACE_STEP: f32 = 2.4;

export const PLACE_Z: f32 = -3.0;

export const PLACE_BASE_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;

export const PLACE_RISE: f32 = 0.5;

// A pure function, exported like a constant: a body of height `h` standing on the floor has its centre at `h / 2`.
export fn half(h: f32) -> f32 {
    return h * 0.5;
}
```

A `prefab` is a reusable entity with parameters and state. An entity can instantiate one (`entity Left: Pillar { ... }`) and a handler can create one at run time with `spawn`:

```mtek
// The Pillar prefab: a box of the given height standing on the floor at `origin`. Its params all have defaults, so
// an instance only says what differs; every default comes from another module.
import { PILLAR_WIDTH, STONE, half } from "../theme.mtek";
import { Matte } from "../materials.mtek";

export prefab Pillar {
    param origin: vec3 = vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
    param height: f32 = 2.0;
    param width: f32 = PILLAR_WIDTH;
    param tint: color = STONE;

    // `origin` is the point on the floor; the box is centred half its height above it. The value reads params and
    // calls an imported function, so the prefab computes it for every instance when the instance is created.
    position: origin + vec3(0.0, half(height), 0.0);
    scale: vec3(width, height, width);
    mesh: Box { size: vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) };
    material: Matte { tint: tint };
}
```

## 9. Physics

Entities with a `body` and a `collider` are simulated. Body kinds and collider shapes are registry schemas (`Dynamic`, `Kinematic`, `Static`; `BoxCollider`, `SphereCollider`); handlers command bodies with `apply_force`, `apply_impulse`, `set_kinematic_target`, `set_linear_velocity`, `teleport` and read `angular_velocity`, `linear_velocity`.

```mtek
    entity Zone {
        position: vec3(4.0, 1.5, 0.0);
        body: Static {};
        collider: BoxCollider { size: vec3(4.0, 2.0, 6.0); sensor: true };

        // `other` is a reference; comparing it with a named entity is allowed, reading its fields is not (E5074).
        on collision_enter(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                entered += 1;
                inside += 1;
            }
        }
        on collision_exit(other: entity_ref) {
            if other != First {
                inside -= 1;
            }
        }
    }
```

The physics engine is a separate module that a program loads only if it uses a body. Its known limitations (no continuous collision detection) are on [limitations](limitations.md).

## 10. Assets

An asset is a compile-time dependency. `asset.glb("path")` opens a binary glTF file while the program is checked; its meshes, materials and node transforms are then read through name-checked accessors, so a misspelled name is a compile error and not a black canvas.

```mtek
export const CHAIR = asset.glb("../models/chair.glb");

// The factors of the model's own materials: the starting values of the configurable inputs.
export const FABRIC_COLOR = CHAIR.material_base_color("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_METALLIC = CHAIR.material_metallic("Fabric");

export const FABRIC_ROUGHNESS = CHAIR.material_roughness("Fabric");
```

The glTF profile of v0.1 is strict (decision 0015): no extensions, no skinning, no animation, one material model. [Limitations](limitations.md) lists each restriction with its diagnostic.

## 11. The tools

The commands of the `mtek` executable are `check`, `build`, `inspect`, `dev`, `new`, `fmt`, `test`, `context`, `grammar`, `lsp`. `mtek check` needs no GPU; `mtek fmt` has one canonical layout and no options; `mtek context` prints this build's supported features for AI agents.

Every diagnostic has a stable code, a message, a span and, when the compiler can prove it, a suggested edit that is re-checked before it is offered. The ranges are in Part D of the reference.
